brief: A hyperreal mechanical watch movement shown open, with jewels, gears and the hairspring. It is rendered only in a narrow ladder of warm paper greys, like an e-ink screen. All tone is built from fine pen stippling and ordered dither dots, with no blended shading anywhere. The background is the pale, slightly yellowed grey of an unlit display. Faint ghosting of a previous image, a second, offset gear, lingers at low contrast. Edges are pixel-crisp and the light is flat and shadowless. It should feel quiet and technical, readable like a page.

A horizontal strip of evenly spaced frames, Muybridge-style, showing a silver coin spinning down onto a black slate. Each frame is hyperreal, with the milled edge, the worn profile portrait and the specular streaks, and it captures the coin progressively tilting until it lies flat. The strip is in graphite and charcoal on warm grey ground, with ruled frame borders and small handwritten-looking index marks. The background is a faint measured grid. Light is cold and clinical, and the sequence reads left to right with scientific detachment.

A hyperreal pile of dried red and orange chillies, with wrinkled skins, split seams and pale seeds. The pile is surrounded by echoing contour bands that step outward like layers of reverse-appliqué cloth. The chillies are rendered in dense coloured pencil and glossy marker. The concentric outline bands are flat watercolour layers in black, scarlet, tangerine and a jolt of turquoise. Each band edge is slightly ragged, like cut fabric, and small slit-shaped gaps reveal the colour beneath. Light is frontal and festive, and the field is filled entirely.

A hyperreal, chipped transferware plate photographed slightly from above on a scrubbed pine table. The glaze crazing, the worn rim gilt and a hairline crack are all visible. The willow scene is drawn only in cobalt and Prussian blue: pagoda, bridge, three figures and two birds. It is laid in fine pen and pale watercolour that blurs slightly, as transfer printing does. The table grain is in warm raw umber washes, the plate's shadow is cool and soft, and morning window light glints across the glaze. The mood is domestic and quiet.

A crushed aluminium soda can lying on asphalt, rendered hyperreal in its dents, torn ink and pooled reflections. The image is built as separate screenprint layers. Flat opaque fills come in fluorescent pink, electric cyan, process yellow and dense black. Coarse spray grain acts as halftone in the gradients. One layer sits slightly out of registration, leaving thin slivers of raw paper and colour fringes along the edges. Ink edges are crisp with occasional squeegee drag. Hard noon light gives a sharp cast shadow, and the mood is pop and gritty.

A hyperreal heap of silver river fish on a banana leaf, with every scale, gill slit and wet eye rendered. The surface is packed edge to edge in the Madhubani manner, with no empty ground. Fine black pen hatching models each scale as a crescent of parallel strokes, and double-line borders of the same pen frame the slab. Flat accents of vermilion, marigold orange and parrot green sit in the leaf veins and the border bands. Light is flat and frontal, like a document. Interest comes from relentless pattern and density, not from depth. It should feel obsessive and handmade.

A strict grid of square compartments, like woven tocapu panels. Each cell holds one hyperreal Andean potato or maize cob: purple, blood-red, ochre-speckled, black-kerneled. Dense coloured-pencil layering builds the skins, the eyes, the soil grit and the waxy kernel highlights. Thin cochineal-red and alpaca-cream bands divide the cells like warp threads. Each compartment has its own small flat background in mustard, slate or terracotta, so the overall field reads as textile from afar and as produce up close. Even overhead light gives the sheet a catalogue calm.

A trompe-l'oeil stage seen from the stalls. A crushed-velvet curtain in carmine and oxblood falls in heavy hyperreal folds, half-drawn to reveal a receding painted backdrop of colonnades. Charcoal-like mass carves the deep shadows in the velvet. Glossy marker glazes catch the gilt proscenium mouldings in raw sienna and bright ochre. Hard footlight comes from below and throws theatrical uplight and long upward shadows. Forced perspective makes the space feel deeper than it is. The edges of the curtain fringe should be crisp enough to touch. The mood is grand, dusty and expectant.

An overhead view of a laterite doorstep at dawn. A freshly drawn kolam of looping white rice-flour lines weaves around a grid of dots, rendered hyperreal. Granular powder edges, scattered grains and smudges where a toe brushed through are all visible. The stone is in dense wet-into-wet watercolour of rust, wet charcoal-brown and slate. The flour lines are crisp, chalky marks that sit on top. The edge of a brass pot and a sliver of a bare foot crop in at the margin. Light is soft pre-sunrise blue.

A hyperreal study of tie-dyed silk scrunched across the whole frame, every bound knot standing up as a tiny puckered crater with its pale resist ring. Soft watercolour washes build the cloth in madder red, turmeric yellow and deep indigo, bleeding at the fold edges the way real dye wicks. Over that, a fine pen stipples each dot-ring and its crinkled thread shadow. The light is low, raking and side-lit, so the knots throw small crescent shadows. The camera is close, the cloth has no horizon, and the dots ripple in rhythmic constellations that warp over each ridge.

An octagonal shadowbox crammed with tiny shells set in concentric rosettes around a heart-shaped centre. Every cowrie, periwinkle and rice shell is rendered hyperreal, with nacre sheen and chipped lips. Delicate coloured pencil carries the shell surfaces in shell-pink, coral, oyster white and pale lilac, with burnished highlights. The hinged mahogany frame is built in warm watercolour glazes. A soft window light from upper left casts small cupped shadows in each shell's mouth. The symmetry is radial and the mood is tender, Victorian and sentimental.

A chrome motorcycle engine drawn as several stacked sheets of tracing paper. The front sheet carries crisp hyperreal pencil rendering of the cooling fins, bolt heads and mirror reflections. Behind it, earlier construction passes show through as softer, slightly offset ghost layers in faded graphite and milky blue-grey watercolour veils. Translucent wash planes act as the paper, layered so their overlaps darken. The composition is off-centre and cropped, with draftsman's ellipse guides still visible. It should feel like process and precision coexisting.

Ketchup and mustard squeeze bottles, a napkin dispenser and a sweating glass of cola sit on a diner counter. The forms and reflections are rendered hyperreal, but each is held inside heavy dark-blue-black outlines like Pont-Aven cloisons. Within the outlines, the colour areas are flat, saturated watercolour fills: tomato red, French's yellow, mint formica and chrome grey. Precise pen details pick out only the condensation beads and logo highlights. Light is a flat neon midday. The contrast between enamel-like flatness and photographic detail should feel deliberate.

A hyperreal slice of cherry pie with a glossy lattice crust and syrupy filling, built entirely from small flat colour facets like a completed paint-by-numbers board. The facet borders are thin and pale, and a few unpainted cells near the edges show faint printed outlines. Saturated marker fills supply the colour: oxblood, scarlet lake, butterscotch, burnt umber and a cool white for the specular glints. Realism emerges only from the sheer number of tiny faceted shapes. The plate sits on a gingham cloth. The mood is kitsch, sweet and uncanny.
